description: The diegetic screens standing in the plaza — pure data the frame source emits as screen slabs and the binder feeds; a screen the world never authors, only declares.

items.description: One diegetic screen in the world — a screen slab emitted by SdfProgramBuilder whose lit face samples a bound source (or the procedural fallback when unbound). The frame (Origin/Right/ Up + HalfWidth/HalfHeight) is the sampled surface frame and must match the slab's placement; the frame source bakes the geometry translate from it.

index.description: The engine screen-surface index (0..MaxScreenSurfaces−1) this slab declares — the key the source/light providers bind under.

origin.description: The front face's world-space center (the sampled surface origin); the geometry center sits one HalfDepth behind it along the face normal.

right.description: The unit world axis the sampled U increases along (the slab's local +X in world space).

up.description: The unit world axis the sampled V increases against — V = 0 at the top (the slab's local +Y in world space).

halfWidth.description: The face half-width (the slab's local X half-extent).

halfHeight.description: The face half-height (the slab's local Y half-extent).

halfDepth.description: The slab's local Z half-extent (its thickness behind the face).

source.description: The signal the lit face carries.

engageable.description: Whether a player may engage this screen.

engageRadius.description: The world-unit radius a player must be inside to engage (meaningful only when Engageable). Validated finite and non-negative.

autoInsert.description: When set, engaging the screen first boots the selected magazine entry (the "walk over, press the button, the screen lights" gesture), so the interaction is one act rather than an insert then an engage.

engageChannel.description: The world-event channel whose arrival on a body engages this screen, or null (the default) for a route that does not answer gestures. The author chooses this name freely; the engine never special-cases a spelling. Omitted from the wire when null.

cycleChannel.description: Same, for advancing the magazine selector. Omitted from the wire when null.

channels.description: The declared channel names this route's mask reaches — a masked-out channel keeps flowing to the routed body's own pose (relevant under the capture:false mirror policy) but never reaches this route's target. null (the default) reaches every declared channel. Omitted from the wire when null.

translation.description: The authored channel→pad-element rows this route's target reads, replacing the engine's default when present. null uses the engine mapping. Omitted from the wire when null.

items.description: One authored channel→pad-element mapping row — a Translation entry.

channel.description: The declared channel name this row reads.

element.description: The neutral pad element the channel's value drives.

solid.description: The screen slab's solidity facet (a box collider derived from the slab's oriented frame + Margin by Server.WorldColliderSet), or null for a decorative screen. Omitted from the wire when null.

magazine.description: The per-screen source magazine (the cycle primitive), or null for a screen with no magazine — nothing to cycle. Omitted from the wire when null — the whole-row UpsertScreen carries it for free, so no new mutation kind is needed.

entries.description: The ordered source list (at least one entry).

items.description: The signal carried by a WorldScreen's lit face. A source declares which provider feeds a slot; the engine resolves and samples it. The $type string is the JSON discriminator; a new source kind is a new derived record plus its JsonDerivedTypeAttribute line.

selected.description: The 0-based entry the selector starts on (what screen.select advances from), not what the screen boots showing — a screen always wakes on its declared Source (the one-live-console ceiling depends on this). Live selection drifts from this and is folded back by world.save (see Puck.World.WorldSessionCapture).

wrap.description: Whether advancing past the last entry returns to the first (the arcade cabinet's wrapping cycle); when false the selector clamps at both ends.
